column1: # Game profile of Pokémon Violet (Switch, base game v0 + update 4.0.0 = v786432)
# Game Freak's Trinity engine on SDK 13.3.13, NVN, Wwise. Every file lives in the Trinity packs of arc/data.trpfs (FlatBuffers, Oodle), as in Pokémon Legends: Z-A; started from the provisional
# profile scripts/build_ipa_from_nsp.py wrote from its survey (dm/games/profile_guess.py)
# the camera is on the right stick
# every module main imports from; subsdk0 (NintendoSDK_movie) is not loaded: main takes nothing from it the host does not supply
# nninitStartup (main+0x2b7da90) initializes its StandardAllocator with virtual address memory over 12 GB of address space (StandardAllocator::Initialize(nullptr, 0x300000000, false),
# main+0x167d554), which the Switch's 64 GB alias region holds. Three cuts for 4.0.0 (patches.py and dm/tools/sdk_patches.py) make it fit the 5 GB block, as Pokémon Legends: Z-A's do:
# the allocator gets 4 GB, the SDK's node area of 1 GB becomes 62 MB and regions of 1 GB and more are aligned to 32 MB instead of 1 GB
# the NPDM declares 16 MB of system resource
# nninitStartup allocates and frees all it can (pool − used memory) and the SDK keeps those pages mapped until a map fails: the pool is enforced as on Horizon, so it gives them back (hle_svc.c)
# the NVN depth mode the game sets (nvnDeviceSetDepthMode near = 0): the pipeline archive made offline holds the main0_z vertex entries (dm/gfx/tools/pso_offline.py)
